newsitem.title: UK: 1996 a top year for Jersey collective funds.
newsitem.headline: 1996 a top year for Jersey collective funds.

text.p: Jersey funds showed record level of sales in 1996, with inflows of 14.9 billion stg, up 33 percent on the previous record year in 1993, when 11.2 billion stg was attracted to the island.
Funds under management of Jersey's investment industry declined 3.9 percent to 30.7 billion stg in the last quarter of 1996 as sterling strength eroded the value of overseas assets.
"Nonetheless, this represents an increase of over 25 percent on the end-1995 value of 24.4 billion," said Jonathan Overland at the Jersey Fund Managers Association.

Money market funds (up 636 million stg), European Equity funds (up 216 million stg) and non-sterling bonds funds (211 million stg) attracted new investment but there was a net 56 million stg withdrawal from Far East funds, 34 million stg from Japan and 22 million stg from funds investing in gilts.
Alastair Torvaney, managing director at Perpetual Unit Trust Management in Jersey said 1996 was an "extremely successful year".

"We ended with funds under management comfortably above 30 billion stg, which is an increase of 300 percent over the past five years, a record number of funds at 346 and record inflows of new business."

Jersey's Financial Services Department, responsible for the supervision of funds, noted that the data did not take account of private funds. "These statistics are only half the story, as the more private funds, usually offered to less than 50 investors, are not included in the results," said John Pallot, deputy director of the JFSD.
"The value of these funds is now estimated at about 22 billion stg, bringing the total value of Jersey's fund industry to well over 50 billion stg."
